newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan OTC index falls for 20th straight session.
newsitem.headline: Japan OTC index falls for 20th straight session.

text.p: Japan's over-the-counter (OTC) index fell for a 20th consecutive session on Friday, extending its longest-ever losing streak.

"Foreign investors were net buyers of OTC stocks but private investors were extremely quiet," the general manager at a second-tier brokerage said. "In such an environment, it is highly unlikely the market will rebound soon."
The index, consisting of many retailers or small companies that rely on domestic business, ended down 2.80 points, or 0.24 percent, at 1,144.28.

The OTC index has been fairly feeble since the start of the calendar year and nearly dropped below the 1,000-point threshold in April. Although it has recovered somewhat from a April 16 closing low of 1,033.86, it is still about 15 percent off the level at which it started 1997.
"Some of the IPOs are gems, but there are just too many coming on board at once, creating a glut in the market," said Tadahiro Kamogawa, general manager at Yamaichi Securities.
"Trading activity in general, even on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, is lacklustre and the fact that there were seven OTC debutants this week did not help," he said.
In the January to mid-July period, more than thirty firms have registered their shares for trade.
Industry sources said that the number of new firms was likely to balloon to more than 100 by the end of the calendar year. Last year 114 firms debuted on the OTC market.

Brokers said underlying concerns about the state of Japan's economy, and when the stifling effect of a rise in the consumption tax would wear off, were also hobbling investor interest in the OTC market. The consumption tax was increase from three to five percent on April 1.
"The mood of the stock market is being set by pricey, global blue chips, especially high technology issues at the moment," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said.
"OTC stocks are upcoming firms involved in domestic businesses and are the complete opposite of what investors who are active now find attractive," he said.
The key market index, the 225-share Nikkei average, closed higher on Friday. It ended up 103.31 points, or 0.51 percent, at 20,389.54.
